diagnostic_evidence.tag: tab: test - Variance of the parameters sets

issues.failure_explanation: Section 4 asserts that the variance of the compensated NTS process is t*delta*Gamma(2-alpha)/lambda^(2-alpha)*(rho*lambda^(1-alpha)+eta*eta^T). The correct value follows from L(t)=B(G(t))-ct with B(s)=eta*s+sqrt(rho)*W(s) and the law of total variance: V[L(t)] = t*(eta*eta^T*V[G(1)] + rho*E[G(1)]) = t*delta*Gamma(2-alpha)/lambda^(2-alpha)*(eta*eta^T + rho*lambda/(1-alpha)), using E[G(1)] = delta*Gamma(1-alpha)/lambda^(1-alpha) and Gamma(2-alpha)=(1-alpha)*Gamma(1-alpha). This is exactly the formula in Appendix A (label 'tab: NTS'), which contradicts the Section 4 display: the two rho-terms coincide only when alpha=0. For the NIG parameter sets (alpha=1/2; e.g. NIG0 with lambda=20766.4) they differ by a large factor (2*lambda=41532.8 versus sqrt(lambda)~=144.1), and the standard deviations and correlation reported in Table 2 for NIG0 (0.1958, 0.1830, 0.8417) match the appendix formula, whereas the Section 4 formula would give approximately 0.0214 and 0.0108. The displayed variance is therefore false for every alpha>0 (all non-VG NTS models, including both NIG sets used in the experiments).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the term rho*lambda^(1-alpha) by rho*lambda/(1-alpha) in the displayed variance in Section 4, making it consistent with Appendix A (label 'tab: NTS') and with the values in Table 2; this is a one-line local correction.
issues.overall_effect: The stated variance of the pure-jump NTS component is wrong for all alpha>0, in particular for the NIG0 and NIG1 parameter sets; any reader using this formula for calibration, moment computations, or to reproduce/verify Table 2 obtains incorrect values. The defect is confined to this displayed claim: Table 2 is computed from the correct appendix formula, and no theorem, algorithm, discretization step, or convergence claim relies on the erroneous expression.
issues.title: Incorrect variance formula for the NTS process in Section 4 (rho*lambda^(1-alpha) instead of rho*lambda/(1-alpha))
issues.why_classification: The defect is a single false displayed formula whose forced correction is available inside the source itself (the appendix formula and the numerically consistent Table 2). Fixing it requires no new argument, no weakening, and no change to any scheme, experiment, or formal result, so every substantive claim and guarantee of the paper is preserved.
